appropriate: a solid ball held in a U-shaped cradle cut from a rounded square reads as 'caught, held' without a caption; calm, enclosing, fits Sage with Caregiver
distinctive: warm amber is unique against the category's blues and greens, but a dot in a rounded square is a generic silhouette (record button, camera, user glyph) none of the five owns yet any could
simple: one rounded square, one U-cut, one circle; describable in a sentence and drawable in seconds
legible: Orvane reads cleanly in every lockup; the dot and cradle still separate at 24 px and 16 px, though the white U gap is near one pixel at 16 px
adaptable: black, reversed white, one-colour 64 and 32, app tile, avatar, dark-header and browser-tab mockups all hold; a ball settling into the cradle gives an obvious motion logic
timeless: no hexagon or gradient, but a circle over a U reads close to the 'V ball' head-and-arms figure trends.md lists under avoid, and a dot-in-ring edges toward concentric
universal: the mirrored panel is identical, but upright it can read as a person/user-profile icon and the rotated-90 panel reads as a C or a Pac-Man shape
clear: unsearched: dot-in-rounded-square marks are common in camera, recording and user-account icons; nothing in webhooks I know of (Svix, Hookdeck, Convoy, Hook0) uses it
congruent: amber hue, symmetry, flat grounded base, medium-heavy weight and softened corners match the targets and the round O; the wordmark is a fairly neutral geometric sans with less humanist warmth than asked
system: horizontal lockup, symbol, ladder 256 to 16 and one-colour tiers derive cleanly; no stacked lockup or distinct favicon redraw shown, rationale not visible on the sheet
